claim: “The two acts are both explicitly expressed in structures like Dick wisely got himself taught the tricks of the trade by David or Ed reluctantly allowed his stepfather to send him to boarding-school.”
evidence_summary: [10iii] (p. 678) is Dick was wisely taught the tricks of the trade by Donald. Footnote 3 (p. 678) and the preceding sentence on p. 679 (“Donald’s teaching him the tricks of the trade”) keep Donald. The companion paraphrase keeps the participants of [10iv], Ed and his stepfather.
proposed_wording: Dick wisely got himself taught the tricks of the trade by Donald
inference: Does the paraphrase keep the example’s participants?

evidence.passage: §3, p. 679. “Dick wisely got himself taught the tricks of the trade by David”.
